title.narrative: Training on child protection for partners in Timor Leste

description.narrative:
CAFOD partners KSI, CDC and CDB support women and men in Timor Leste to be able to make a decent living and meet the needs of themselves and their families in ways that are sustainable, for example through training groups to promote agricultural diversification and improving the access groups have to markets.
Each partner recognises that there are risks involved in providing livelihoods training to community members, for example when members of the groups bring their children to the trainings and expose them to potentially dangerous machinery, or when parents send children to local fairs during school hours to sell the groups’ produce, or when faced with young girl brides wanting to join the groups to making a living for their new families.
KSI, CDC and CDB attended a CAFOD/Plan child protection training in June 2011, however no follow-up support was provided and to date the organisations have yet to develop child protection policies. This means that staff members still lack clarity on how to act when presented with situations such as the above, to ensure children are not harmed as a result of their activities. Each organisation recognises that their staff should be aware of the potential challenges and dangers that arise when children become exposed to/involved in their work.
Therefore CAFOD is organising a 3-day training in Baucau in September 2013, facilitated by a Child Protection Trainer from Plan Indonesia. From this training, each organisation will be (re)introduced to child protection issues, will develop a draft child protection policy relevant for their organisation, and will be trained on training their colleagues on the new policy.
